headline: Devon-Coterra platform delivers a step-change quarter
summary_short: Devon Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.42B (+73.2% y/y) and diluted EPS of $2.03 (+44.0% y/y), its first full quarter as the combined Devon-Coterra platform after the merger closed May 7. Operating cash flow was $3.67B and capex ran $1.27B, 2% below guidance midpoint.
summary_long: Revenue, net income, cash flow, equity and share count all stepped up sharply after the May 7 Coterra Energy merger close, so q/q and y/y deltas on these lines reflect consolidation, not organic growth. Oil production of 503 kbd hit the top of guidance on strong Delaware Basin well performance; capex of $1.27B ran 2% under the guidance midpoint. Cash fell to $950M (-46.1% q/q) after Devon funded a $2.6B New Mexico lease acquisition, retired $500M of term loan/senior notes, and returned $1.06B to shareholders via a 33%-higher $0.32/share dividend and buybacks ($197M). Total debt rose to $11.4B. Full-year 2026 guidance is unchanged from June; Q3 guidance calls for 1,660-1,690 kboe/d production, 550-560 kbd oil, $1,400-1,500M capex.

drivers.explanation: Reflects consolidated operations following the May 7 close of the Coterra Energy merger plus strong oil realizations of $88.09/bbl on robust crude benchmark pricing; not comparable to pre-merger standalone periods.
Ran 2% below the guidance midpoint, primarily attributable to timing and effective cost management.

Share count rose in the same quarter Devon closed its merger with Coterra Energy (May 7); the release does not itemize the share-issuance mechanics separately, but the timing coincides with the combination.

First full quarter as the combined Devon-Coterra platform: oil production of 503 kbd reached the top end of guidance, capex ran 2% under midpoint, and the company returned $1.06B to shareholders via a 33%-higher dividend, renewed buybacks and debt retirement, while full-year 2026 guidance stays unchanged from June.
